channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
item.description: WIS-MeZO replaces MeZO's dense random perturbations in zeroth-order fine-tuning with sparse perturbations restricted to coordinates selected by Wanda weight-activation saliency, while keeping the pretrained weights dense. It adds a one-time saliency computation and mask construction, requires storing a sparse mask, and retains ZO's multiple forward passes per step; claimed benefit is fewer optimization steps to reach comparable validation loss. It can fail if the saliency-ranked support captures insufficient gradient energy for a given task, if the task-conditioning assumption breaks under distribution shift, or if sparse-gather overhead erodes the step-count savings in a memory-bound forward-only pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
item.description: Deep DualMamba replaces Transformer-based attention and MLP layers with an adaptive bidirectional state-space architecture plus a hardware-aware parallel recurrent algorithm. It reduces asymptotic complexity to linear in sequence length at the cost of implementing and validating a custom parallel scan operator and accepting the loss of convolutional efficiency the authors explicitly note. Long-term forecasting can still fail because the method is evaluated only on UK meteorological-station data, the claimed robustness is supported by a single domain, and the abstract supplies no error metrics, baseline deltas, or throughput measurements. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
item.description: DRAMA replaces full-sequence bidirectional attention over all visual tokens with Spatial-Redundancy-Aware Visual Token Pruning (SVTP) and Sufficiency-Guided Adaptive Stopping (SGAS). It requires no training, architectural modification, or attention caching, but introduces inference-time computation for probing attention tensors and dynamic token selection. Accuracy may degrade on benchmarks where the sparse visual token subset or early stopping criteria fail to capture necessary information. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation
item.description: It replaces fine-tuning a large multilingual foundation model with a small BART pre-trained from scratch on domain monolingual text, augmented via rule-based transforms, masked substitution, back-translation, and one-shot prompting. The cost is assembling monolingual corpora, building an annotated parallel set (here 1,000 pairs expanded to 4,831), running a from-scratch pre-training phase, and accepting that full fine-tuning—not LoRA—is needed to preserve quality. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on BdSL gloss translation with a small evaluation set, BLEU gains may not transfer to other low-resource tasks or languages, and the augmentation pipeline can introduce label noise. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
item.description: CoMem replaces indiscriminate soft context compression (which encodes all content into fixed memory slots regardless of query) with a query-conditioned compressor trained via contrastive learning on same-document negative queries, using bidirectional attention among memory slots. It costs training a compressor model with specialized hard-negative mining (pairing documents with multiple queries), adds inference-time query encoding before compression, and requires maintaining bidirectional attention infrastructure. It can fail when queries arrive after compression (the method assumes query availability at compression time), when training data lacks sufficient query diversity to learn robust selectivity, or when the compressor discards evidence needed for unanticipated query patterns. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: The method replaces scalar-reward RL that discards trial traces, and replaces hand-crafted reflection/playbook scaffolds, by learning the action, reflection, and curation roles jointly under a fixed harness, evaluating artifacts by their downstream effect on future rollouts. It costs full RL training over a multi-role LLM pipeline: environment rollouts, reward infrastructure, and training capacity that exceed a single 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. It can fail through reward hacking of downstream effect evaluation, playbook drift where learned artifacts encode spurious patterns, and non-transfer of the trained scaffold behaviors to tasks outside the benchmark distribution. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency
item.description: It replaces indiscriminate activation of reasoning, RAG, web search, and calculator capabilities on every query with a small Qwen2.5 router (1.5B-14B) making four independent routing decisions via prompt optimization. The cost is router inference overhead, which grows with router capacity and was measured in a separate environment, plus the effort of capability-specific prompt tuning and maintaining labeled routing data. Failures are capability-dependent: false-positive activations waste compute without quality loss, while false negatives on RAG and web search degrade answer quality, and similar classification F1 scores can hide these divergent downstream effects. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SoScale: Second-Order Scale Search for FP4 Quantization
item.description: SoScale replaces default maximum-absolute-value scaling and element-wise reconstruction error minimization for FP4 quantization scale selection. It requires computing Hessian information and performing GPTQ-style error recovery during the search, increasing offline quantization time and implementation complexity compared to standard calibration. The method depends on calibration data representativeness; if the Hessian approximation is poor or the calibration distribution mismatches production traffic, the selected scales may fail to preserve accuracy on actual inputs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving
item.description: The method replaces direct supervised fine-tuning on theorem-proving data with a 33.7B-token agent-native mid-training phase plus roughly 36K verifier-grounded agent trajectories collected through a custom Lean-interaction harness. It costs multi-billion-token mid-training compute, a formal-verifier sandbox infrastructure, and trajectory-collection effort, none of which fit a single 24 GB GPU or a limited cloud budget. It can fail if the synthesized corpus or trajectories are not released, and its gains are demonstrated only for Lean theorem proving, with no evidence of transfer to general production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
item.description: The kit replaces reliance on a single noisy hosted competition score and ad-hoc local testing with a local evaluator that sandboxes agent-written code in network-isolated containers, verifies conformance with the hosted scorer's prompts down to rendered tokens, and applies paired statistics that respect repository clustering. It costs container-orchestration infrastructure, maintenance of conformance checks as the hosted scorer evolves, and the compute to run hundreds of evaluations (about 250 runs per hour for a 4B agent on one high-end GPU), plus engineering effort to integrate one's own agent bundle. It can fail because the paper's own experiments show that screen-passing agent changes did not confirm on new tasks and that 65% of tasks were solved in none of eight baseline runs, so an adopted kit can still mislead if users underpower their comparisons or over-trust single-run gains. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing
item.description: It replaces single overall-recall scoring and loosely generated trajectories with a six-tier diagnostic benchmark built mostly from real production trajectories, including benign lookalike cases and paired shortened or information-supplemented variants. It costs benchmark access plus the compute or API budget to run candidate auditors against it, and it provides no direct inference, memory, or quality improvement to a deployed agent. It can fail if its selected scenarios do not match the reader's deployment distribution, if teams tune auditors to the six tiers rather than to real risk coverage, or if the missed-risk patterns it exposes are not actionable within a small team's auditing stack. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
item.description: The study challenges the default of delegating subtasks to secondary LLM agents, positioning direct tool use by a single orchestrating LLM as the stronger baseline. Multi-agent delegation adds orchestration complexity and extra API calls, and the paper finds no consistent accuracy gain for that cost. Delegated pipelines can fail through distorted delegated queries, inefficient tool use, and loss of information between agents, especially on post-cutoff knowledge tasks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
item.description: Singularity-Bench replaces narrow agent evaluations and the conventional Harbor framework with six end-to-end autonomous AI-development tasks and Breakwater, a Harbor extension hardened against reward hacking across nine OWASP agentic categories. It costs substantial evaluation infrastructure, identical-hardware human baselines, red-teaming effort, and frontier-model access rather than a simple drop-in metric. It can fail if benchmark tasks do not transfer to the reader's production workflows, if Breakwater's attack coverage misses new exploits, or if results from frontier models do not generalize to smaller self-hosted systems. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Folio: Recoverable Multi-Resolution Context Folding for Long-Horizon Language Agents
item.description: Folio replaces model-written summarization-based context compaction with a programmatic fold over three pre-existing linked views (model-written turn notes, a runtime event manifest, and full source records), printing handles so bounded recovery tools can re-read evidence on demand. It adds per-reply turn-note generation and persistent storage of event manifests and source records, plus recovery tooling and a dossier, but removes the inference cost and latency of each compaction pass (median fold 0.6 s). It can fail when turn notes omit details later needed, when handle-based retrieval returns the wrong evidence, or when the fold trigger's landing-point pricing misfires on workloads with irregular token growth. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
item.description: The method replaces naive batch admission and static GPU-memory partitioning in agent rollout systems with workload-based KV-cache/recurrent-state allocation, trajectory-aware routing for cache reuse, and Chain-Advancing Action Scheduling that prioritizes long trajectories to shorten the batch tail. The cost is engineering complexity: it requires a resource model for hybrid LLM memory, routing and scheduling logic, and a controlled-replay harness for validation, all tightly coupled to the serving stack. It can fail when the workload does not exhibit long-chain skew or reusable prefixes (the gains vanish), when environment capacity rather than GPU compute is the bottleneck, or when the scheduling heuristics mispredict progress and starve short tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MobileProbe: Adaptive Security Evaluation of Mobile Agents via Trajectory-Aware Injection
item.description: MobileProbe replaces fixed-point, hand-crafted injection benchmarks with an adaptive pipeline that discovers attackable UI surfaces via automated pentesting, locates vulnerable decision points along the agent's actual trajectory, and evolves context-aware payloads through a surrogate-filtered loop. Adopting it requires standing up an instrumented mobile app environment, a surrogate filtering model, and an evolutionary payload-generation loop, which is a substantial engineering investment beyond simple API evaluation on a 24 GB GPU. It can fail when attacker-controllable surfaces are missed during pentesting, when the surrogate filter misranks payloads, or when results on 12 apps and three agent architectures do not transfer to the reader's deployment. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Towards Green Text Generation: Memory-Based Speculative Decoding
item.description: Replaces a neural draft model (e.g., TinyLlama) in speculative decoding with a CPU-based memory classifier that predicts the next token from a four-token window, using no GPU, no backpropagation, and no accelerator memory. Cost is a domain-matched memory model that must be built per domain, sub-millisecond CPU inference, and acceptance rates (38.1% on legal text) well below neural drafters, which limits gains when the verifier is already KV-cached. It can fail on out-of-domain text where the memory classifier's acceptance collapses, and the energy-optimal draft length differs from the speed-optimal one, so naive configuration can raise energy without improving throughput. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
item.description: The method replaces traditional window-based and envelope-curve monitoring of screwdriving processes with a VQ-VAE embedding-space anomaly detector plus deep classifiers over torque and rotation-angle time series. It costs a labeled industrial sensor dataset, training and validation effort for several architectures, and integration into manufacturing process monitoring, none of which involves LLM inference or foundation-model infrastructure. It can fail on real-world data distributions that differ from the training corpus, and the reported 100% accuracy likely reflects a controlled setup that may not transfer across screw types, tools, or production lines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Detection Is Not Early Warning: Evaluating Token-Level Alarms on Language Model Failures
item.description: The method replaces response-level AUROC evaluation of failure monitors with PREWARN, a protocol that calibrates monitor thresholds on validation data and scores alarms relative to annotated failure onsets, distinguishing classification, detection, and early warning. It requires failure data with annotated onsets, adds a calibration step and per-token alarm scoring, and released calibrated linear probes keep inference cost low, though low-rank adapters below the probe add modest training and inference overhead. It can fail when onsets cannot be annotated for the target failure, when validation calibration does not transfer to production traffic, or when early warnings still arrive too close to the onset to permit intervention, and the case study covers only repetitive degeneration in three open models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Outcome-Mass Alignment: Controlling Length-Dependent Trajectory Influence in Multi-Turn LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: OMA replaces the implicit weighting rule in stepwise group-relative multi-turn RL by computing outcome statistics over unique source trajectories and controlling aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation, without changing the base optimizer's credit assignment, importance ratios, or clipping. It adds modest accounting complexity and requires tracking trajectory expansion and outcome coupling, but it does not introduce a new training-stage dependency or obvious inference cost. It can fail when expansion does not couple to outcomes, as the paper reports mixed or reversed effects on ordinary WebShop, so gains are workload-dependent rather than universal. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Locality Meets Interference: Structure and Scheduling in Radio Multicasting
item.description: This paper analyzes distributed scheduling and coloring algorithms for multipoint-to-multipoint multicasting in synchronous radio networks, replacing ad hoc or naive broadcast transmission schemes in distributed systems. It costs significant algorithmic complexity and requires assumptions like synchronous slots, distance-two coloring, or geometric data, with performance bounded by network parameters like diameter d and degree Delta_0. Adoption can fail if the reader's infrastructure lacks the required model assumptions, and it is irrelevant to AI/ML production workloads involving model inference, training, or data processing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Sustainable Federated Fine-Tuning with LoRA: Environmental Impact and Performance Footprint
item.description: The method replaces standard federated fine-tuning configurations that use higher local step counts (100) with a constrained budget (10 steps) while applying LoRA to LLMs. It requires implementing federated averaging infrastructure and accepting that the energy-optimal configuration depends on specific hardware and model scale; the observed 6-8x energy reduction applies specifically to the tested 135M-360M parameter range on A40 and RTX 6000 Ada GPUs. Extrapolating these efficiency gains to larger foundation models or different hardware architectures may not hold, and reducing local steps could alter convergence dynamics in ways not captured by the tested accuracy metrics. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
item.description: STEALTH replaces bit-exact provably secure linguistic steganography, which requires sender and receiver to reproduce identical token probabilities, with an exponential-race token sampler plus a rateless spinal code decoded by beam search that tolerates probability mismatches across precision, quantization, hardware, tokenizers, and model families. The cost is added encoding/decoding complexity (keyed pseudorandom sampling, beam-search spinal decoding) and a lower effective payload than idealized bit-exact schemes, since redundancy absorbs token flips. Adoption can fail if the threat model shifts, if stronger steganalyzers emerge, or if the receiver's distribution diverges so far that race flips exceed the code's correction capacity, and cross-family robustness is empirical rather than guaranteed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
item.description: S1-Evo replaces generic prompt-injection or override attacks with contract-aware perturbations of untrusted fields that compete with task evidence against typed S1 scorers, using offline margin-guided search and retrieval of 'experience cards' at test time. Cost is an offline seed-task optimization loop with re-verification plus a card store and retrieval step at inference; it adds no parameters to the production model but adds attack-side compute and pipeline complexity. It can fail when margin feedback is unavailable or coarse-grained, when retrieved cards do not transfer to unseen task distributions, and when deployed S1 interfaces add input sanitization or contract validation not modeled by the framework. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Lara Mini Base: Language Diversity as a Resource, Not a Trade-off
item.description: Lara Mini Base replaces the standard dense multilingual base model with a Mixture of Experts architecture (7.2B total, 0.6B active parameters) to mitigate capacity competition between languages. It costs the complexity of serving an MoE model and memory for 7.2B parameters (approximately 14.4 GB in bfloat16, leaving limited headroom on a 24 GB GPU for the 128k context KV cache), while adoption is further restricted by the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial license. Potential failure modes include underperformance in languages outside its 45 supported languages, long-context memory exhaustion, and degradation on tasks requiring alignment tuning since this is a base model. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
item.description: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on analog circuit layout design, replacing ad-hoc or manual assessment of agent performance in this domain. It costs computational resources and domain expertise to run the benchmark's verification and quality metrics. Failures can occur due to the complexity of physical constraints and iterative design tasks, leading to low success rates in generating valid layouts. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
item.description: The method replaces static general-purpose skill libraries with per-user Adapters that encode local adjustments, plus a routing agent that maintains an online task-level skill library and preloads candidates for later subtasks. The cost is an additional RL training loop for two decision policies, an adapter storage and routing layer, and runtime overhead for candidate preloading and applicability rechecking. It can fail when user-specific adjustments are sparse or noisy, when the routing agent mis-selects under expanding pools, and when the RL optimization overfits to benchmark feedback signals rather than production execution traces. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
item.description: This is a measurement and survey framework for verifiable AI using zero-knowledge proofs, not a deployable inference optimization; it replaces nothing in the reader's stack. It clarifies that proof-generation costs shift across proof systems and input lengths, that a 13B-parameter fine-tuning proof configuration exceeds a 40GB GPU and requires 80GB, and that kernel limits involve instruction issue and synchronization rather than bandwidth alone. For the reader, applying zkML proving would add substantial prover compute, memory, and integration complexity and can fail on GPU capacity or proof-system-specific bottlenecks, while typical production inference does not require cryptographic verification. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: AURA 2.0: From User-Driven Responses to Model-Initiated Conversations in Streaming Video
item.description: The method replaces purely reactive, user-prompted video assistants with a model that initiates conversations, calls tools with stream context, grounds outputs in bounding boxes, and maintains long-horizon memory, requiring a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and a three-stage training scheme. Adoption costs include fine-tuning or at minimum deploying a specialized streaming video LLM, plus orchestration for tool calls, frame-aligned grounding, and memory state, all of which add serving complexity on a single 24 GB GPU. Failure modes include mistimed or unwanted proactive interruptions, incorrect tool invocations from visual context, grounding errors on user-marked regions, and memory drift over long streams. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Discovering Effective Agent Memory Designs through Program Evolution
item.description: MAPE replaces manually engineered agent memory architectures with an evolutionary search that discovers memory programs from minimal seeds. The primary costs are the search-phase compute budget and increased system complexity, though the discovered designs can shift computation from expensive memory construction to cheaper query-time processing. Adoption can fail if the evolved programs overfit to the evaluation benchmarks or if the search cost exceeds available resources. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
item.description: This regime replaces full fine-tuning and teacher-trace reasoning supervision with parameter-efficient LoRA trained on labels alone. It requires only single-GPU-scale training memory and avoids the cost of generating teacher traces, though a teacher model is needed if reasoning variants are compared; the tradeoff is that adding reasoning supervision underperforms labels-only training in-domain. What can fail is that results are demonstrated on Qwen3-8B financial tasks only, so the ranking may not transfer to other base models, domains, or tasks where explicit reasoning is required at inference. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Joint Null-Space Projection for Data-Free Model Merging
item.description: JNSP replaces entry-wise merging heuristics (averaging, TIES, Task Arithmetic) with a closed-form projection that removes from each task vector the components lying in other tasks' top-r right-singular subspaces. It costs one SVD per two-dimensional weight tensor per task, requires no data, forward passes, or training, and is order-independent, so it runs comfortably on constrained infrastructure. It can fail outside the validated setting: on RoBERTa-large it underperforms plain Task Arithmetic, and a sequential variant collapses to 69.6%, so the specific joint formulation matters. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Paper-Faithful Federated Learning: Scientific Checks for Practitioner and Agent Development
item.description: FedBrew replaces ad hoc federated learning experiment scripts with a controlled codebase that verifies partitions, aggregation weights, checkpoint recovery, and run records. It costs integration and maintenance effort, adds runtime check overhead, and imposes a prescriptive experimental structure. It cannot detect semantic mismatches outside its specified checks, and its benefits are limited if production FL is not in scope. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Parsed, Plausible, Wrong: Output Format Controls Silent Errors in Small-Model Semantic Parsing
item.description: It replaces terse symbolic target formats (e.g., s-expressions) in LoRA fine-tuning of sub-billion parsers with a lossless plain-words encoding of the same tree, at no extra infrastructure cost and with 4.1x fewer output tokens. The cost is a measured strict-refusal trade-off: 2.1-10.1% of real, mostly polite, orders are rejected, and adopting the format requires retraining on re-encoded targets. It can fail because evidence comes from a single benchmark (PIZZA ordering), shortening alone never helped, so gains may not transfer to other domains, schemas, or models. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off
item.description: The technique modifies standard LoRA training by adding a differentiable Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss, replacing the usual practice of relying on unpenalized low-rank updates that often underuse their configured rank. It costs additional training-time regularization and hyperparameter tuning, with the paper reporting that mean training perplexity improves or increases by at most 0.02 in all but one model-rank comparison, but it does not establish a serving-time advantage. It can fail if the workload is single-task, if the chosen λ or rank does not match the domain mix, or if the capacity gain does not translate into better downstream retention outside the tested settings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Sparse Convolution
item.description: This method replaces standard dense convolution with a direct sparse convolution algorithm designed to exploit high weight sparsity resulting from pruning. It requires implementing custom sparse kernels and handling irregular memory access patterns, which increases engineering complexity compared to using standard dense libraries. Adoption can fail if the model's sparsity is too low or unstructured, as the overhead of sparse indexing may negate the computational savings, or if existing vendor libraries already optimize the specific workload effectively. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sheaf-Inspired Structured Scoring Extensions of LightGCN for Collaborative Filtering
item.description: Replaces the identity inner-product scorer in a three-layer LightGCN backbone with structured pair-dependent transformations including diagonal, rank-one low-rank, or full matrix residual scorers. Adds parameter-matched computational overhead and architectural complexity without a demonstrated causal benefit from the underlying sheaf geometry. Dataset-dependent ranking improvements may not generalize, and coverage gains can vary substantially across domains. 2 independent implementations, 35 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
item.description: LiveGeo replaces static, fixed-state geographic reasoning benchmarks with a continuously evolving environment (GeoWorld) that forces agents to actively acquire evidence, re-verify prior decisions, and revise plans. The cost is infrastructure and evaluation complexity: it requires running a stateful, temporally evolving world with verifiable state histories, which is heavier than standard static prompt-response evaluation and does not itself yield a production-ready capability. What can fail is that strong static performance does not transfer to dynamic reliability, and the identified bottleneck—acquiring and translating evidence into valid decisions over time—means the benchmark mainly diagnoses weaknesses rather than providing an adoptable mechanism to fix them. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Where LLM Agents Get Stuck Debugging Databases: Access More Than Reasoning
item.description: Replaces unrestricted production database access for debugging agents with a controlled forensics layer: a safe interrogation API, lock-and-deadlock flight recorder, and production replay harness inside existing security controls. Costs engineering effort to build and maintain these interfaces, adds latency to evidence gathering compared with direct access, and requires continuous updates as schemas and security policies evolve. Can fail if the forensics layer still omits incident-critical runtime state, if security teams reject the access model, or if agents draw confident conclusions from incomplete evidence despite the added instrumentation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
item.description: The technique replaces ad-hoc, heuristic memory writing between successive coding tasks with prospective segment valuation, anchor-based compact memory (repository locations and executable checks), and on-policy actor training that credits memory-using steps. It costs a training pipeline (paired runs with and without segments, grouped rollouts, provenance-gated value credit), plus ongoing memory-module calls whose token overhead is partially offset by fewer steps. It can fail because the method depends on training a specific actor (27B in the paper) with a custom reward, gains are demonstrated only on a single 4.7-point benchmark improvement, and no open-source implementation or transfer evidence to other models or repositories is provided. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
item.description: The technique replaces the discontinued, proprietary Xilinx ISE 14.7 toolchain for Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 FPGAs with an open-source, browser-based flow using Yosys and nextpnr. Its primary costs are the engineering effort to integrate it and the risk of using unmeasured device features, which the system is designed to refuse. Failure can occur if a design requires a device feature that has not been black-box measured and added to the flow's database, or if subtle, undetected hardware incompatibilities exist. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
item.description: Ask2Decide is a 43-task benchmark that replaces uncalibrated LLM-simulated users with solver-verified, human-calibrated operator interactions to test whether planning agents ask for missing facts that actually change optimal plans. Adopting it costs human interaction collection and solver setup rather than compute, and it diagnoses but does not fix the problem: frontier models still produce infeasible plans on 58-98% of under-specified tasks. It can fail as a proxy because 43 tasks and 79 sessions from 19 participants limit statistical power and may not transfer to a specific production domain. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
item.description: The method replaces direct VLM reading or OCR of degraded user screenshots by augmenting the coding agent with crisp screenshots rendered from the repository under modification, requiring no bug-free version or manual annotation. Costs include a rendering pipeline for reproducible application states (build, launch, screenshot automation), additional image tokens in the context, and infrastructure to keep rendered states current with the repository. It can fail when the application cannot be rendered automatically, when the bug manifests only under user-specific state absent from the rendered reference, or when the injected-bug benchmark does not transfer to real bug reports. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
item.description: Replaces heuristic or reference-free selection of successful trajectories in multi-turn on-policy distillation with an LCS-based compatibility assignment. Costs additional computation to align action sequences between failed and successful trajectories, but requires no architectural changes or extra model parameters. Can fail when the LCS proxy does not capture true latent state compatibility, leading to misleading supervision from incompatible references. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation
item.description: Replaces manual algorithm optimization in numerical libraries with automated LLM-driven rewriting and redesign. Costs include computational resources for iterative agent loops and the need to implement domain-specific verifiers. Can fail if the agent generates code that passes verifiers but produces incorrect physical results on edge cases. 1 independent implementation, 11 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces hand-written or model-agnostic prompt procedures with reusable skills authored by a teacher LLM that profiles the specific student, probes its failures, and admits skills only after validated improvement on matched development tasks. Costs teacher-side API calls for profiling, diagnostic probing, and admission testing, plus a deployment route that injects the library into the student's context, all of which fit a single-GPU or API budget. Gains are student-specific: libraries transfer poorly across models, a student that cannot follow instructions negates the benefit, and misleading learner profiles cause all candidate skills to fail admission. 5 independent implementations, 162 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
item.description: The approach replaces single-shot prompting of LLMs for low-resource enterprise DSLs with an execution-graded loop in which the model compiles its output, receives errors, and edits iteratively, supplemented by carefully worded domain guidance. Costs are additional inference calls per task (higher token spend and latency), plus engineering effort to build the compile-feedback harness and to author and tune skill documentation; the paper also shows packaging guidance as a live plugin can halve its value (28% as documentation versus 14% as a plugin) unless the skill wording is rewritten. Failure modes include the loop not recovering from fundamental knowledge gaps (all models scored 0% on authoring from scratch), sensitivity to how guidance is phrased and delivered, and results that may not transfer beyond the proprietary Salesforce AgentScript setting in which they were measured. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
item.description: The method replaces implicit agent coordination scattered across prompts, tool calls, and application code with explicit BPMN process models compiled into a LangGraph/Pregel runtime, where LLM reasoning is confined to designated agentic tasks and deterministic gateways handle control flow, approvals, and system calls. Its costs are process-modeling effort, dependence on BPMN tooling (SemTalk) plus the LangGraph stack, and added engineering complexity to maintain models, ontologies, and knowledge graphs alongside the agents. It can fail when business processes are too dynamic to model accurately, when models drift from actual execution behavior, or when the orchestration overhead outweighs the monitoring and reusability benefits for small workflows. 2 independent implementations, 139 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement across Seven Open Reasoning Models
item.description: Replaces the invisible default of forwarding stripped reasoning histories across providers by a two-cell screen (one retention run, one deletion run) that yields a per-model sensitivity reading used as prior information in routing and aggregation. Costs two evaluation runs per model and a small routing-table entry; no extra GPU, training, or serving overhead. Can fail if a model is retrained or re-released, since the reading is model-level and must be re-measured for each new version. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: FlowPlan: Reducing the Token Cost of Coding Agents with Abstraction-Guided Planning and Verification
item.description: FlowPlan replaces the coding agent's iterative loop of re-reading raw source and re-running tests after each edit with localization, explicit repair planning as graph deltas on per-function control-flow or data-flow graphs, and a structural comparison of planned versus observed changes followed by a final verification. The cost is the engineering required to build and maintain per-language graph extraction and delta-comparison tooling plus extra planning steps, which adds complexity and may add latency per repair even as total tokens fall. It can fail where the abstraction mislocalizes the fault, where the planned graph delta does not capture the needed semantic change, or where gains shrink with stronger models, as the Sonnet 5 results (0.72-0.94x) show much smaller savings than Haiku. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
item.description: EC-SWE replaces ad hoc or contamination-prone agent evaluations (e.g., SWE-bench-style saturated benchmarks) with 100 calibrated, expert-authored multi-file tasks featuring weighted executable graders, must-pass blockers, and adversarial control patches. It costs nothing to adopt directly since it is an evaluation artifact, not a deployable method; using it meaningfully requires running frontier API models in a full platform harness, which exceeds a small team's budget at 3,495 scored runs. What can fail is selection bias: the 76 held-out tasks prevent independent verification, and scores measured against provider-native tool interfaces may not transfer to the reader's own constrained tooling or domain. 1 independent implementation, 30 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
item.description: This replaces symptom-level failure labeling (failure-mode tags, responsible-agent attribution) with a structured episode record that traces each fault's origin, propagation, detection, response, and consequence, and it motivates adopting specific runtime controls: independent evidence-reading judges, task contracts fixed at admission, and environment-grounded belief re-checks. The cost is primarily engineering complexity and extra inference calls for the judge/verification layers, plus increased latency and API spend per run, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or via third-party APIs without training. Adoption can fail because the empirical base is only 95 failed runs from two public corpora of multi-agent systems, so the reach and effectiveness of the proposed controls may not transfer to single-agent or different-domain workloads, and judge-based controls can themselves introduce LLM errors. 3 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Project Progress Desk: Know Where All Your Claude Code and Codex Projects Stand at a Glance
item.description: Replaces manual switching between chat windows, terminal sessions, and provider interfaces with a unified local desktop view that tracks progress, blockers, and pending decisions across parallel coding projects. Costs implementation effort to integrate agent receipts and weighted acceptance checklists into the local environment, plus ongoing maintenance as agent APIs evolve. Can fail if the acceptance checklists are poorly defined or if receipt parsing produces false positives that misrepresent actual completion status. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MRFoundry: Knowledge-guided agent loops for end-to-end MRI research
item.description: MRFoundry replaces ad-hoc prompting of general-purpose coding agents for MRI research tasks with a package of domain knowledge, tool integrations, project-local memory, and output checks. It costs integration effort with existing agent frameworks, dependency on third-party LLM APIs, and maintenance of domain guidance, with no direct GPU or training cost. It can fail on tasks outside its curated guidance, its Hard-task success rate remains below 45%, and gains depend on the underlying model and the quality of contributed domain knowledge. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: PegasusAI Studio: Legible Cyberinfrastructure and Accountable AI Agents for Scientific Workflows
item.description: PegasusAI Studio replaces ad-hoc, unauthenticated use of coding agents against shared cyberinfrastructure with a curated knowledge base, runtime introspection, and per-user credential scoping so that every agent action is attributed and bounded. The cost is substantial integration: it presupposes a Pegasus/HTCondor deployment, federated authentication, JupyterHub or Open OnDemand hosting, and facility-curated knowledge bases, none of which exist on a single 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. Failure modes include stale facility knowledge misleading the agent, approval-control gaps for state-changing actions, and mis-scoped scheduler credentials if the trust envelope is misconfigured. 1 independent implementation, 11 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
item.description: Replaces manual, evolutionary, or expert-driven search for exchange-correlation functional forms in density functional theory with frontier LLM agents connected via the Model Context Protocol to a GPU-based fitting and validation pipeline. Cost: access to frontier API-based LLMs, a domain-specific DFT evaluator with self-consistent and external benchmarks (GSCDB137, MGCDB84), and the engineering to couple these via MCP; compute is modest per fit but requires roughly 400 fits per search and physics-aware infrastructure. Failure modes: gains may not survive self-consistency or external evaluation, symbolic forms may lack physical content or transferability, agent search may not outperform evolutionary baselines reliably, and results depend heavily on backbone choice and evaluation protocol. 2 independent implementations, 139 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
item.description: Veritas replaces hand-written task verifiers with automatically generated ones, using an evidence header, a domain-rule library, and authoring principles refined by a self-improvement loop. The cost is additional LLM calls for verifier generation plus maintaining the rule library and generation pipeline, and gains are measured as agreement with official verdicts rather than end-task quality. It can fail where generated verifiers encode incorrect or incomplete domain rules, where agreement with official benchmarks does not transfer to the reader's own tasks, or where self-improvement refinement drifts without ground-truth checks. 4 independent implementations, 33 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders
item.description: The method replaces per-layer and per-round KV caching in looped language models with an asymmetric causal encoder-decoder in which a recurrently looped encoder refines a single globally shared KV cache via stochastic-depth training to a fixed point, eliminating round-wise cache growth. The cost is a full architecture change and a training procedure with stochastic recurrence depth, which is incompatible with simply reusing an existing pretrained decoder-only checkpoint and adds training complexity. It can fail if the fixed-point equilibrium does not hold for a given task or depth distribution, degrading long-context quality, and the serving numbers were validated only at 552B-parameter scale on a 4xGB200 node, so benefits at smaller scales are unverified. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The AI Era's Lines of Code? A Case Study on What an Engineer's Token Spend Measures
item.description: This is an observational measurement study, not a deployable technique; it replaces nothing directly but argues against using token spend as a proxy for productivity, recommending instead task- and outcome-based evaluation of agent-assisted work. The cost of adopting its recommendation is the engineering effort to instrument task-level and outcome metrics instead of relying on readily available token billing data. What can fail: token spend correlates only weakly with output (doubling spend associated with ~10% more commits; available metrics explain 13% of within-engineer variation), so budgeting or performance decisions based on it can misallocate resources and penalize efficient users. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
item.description: SteerDistill replaces standard post-training quantization (PTQ) or quantized LoRA methods that treat behavioral drift as a static weight-approximation problem. It requires a full-precision teacher model and an iterative training loop where the teacher steers the student through rollouts to correct environment-specific failures, adding significant complexity to the training pipeline. Adoption may fail if the full-precision teacher cannot accurately guide the student in specific environmental contexts or if the student lacks the capacity to internalize steered behaviors without guidance. 4 independent implementations, 162 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving
item.description: It replaces unbounded admission and simple throttling in prefix-cached agent serving (vLLM/SGLang) with a budgeter that caps the resident KV demand of active sessions to the KV pool, suspending admitted sessions when over capacity. The cost is queued or suspended sessions (added tail latency for held work) plus modest scheduler complexity; no extra hardware is required, and a CPU offload tier alone is shown to be insufficient. What can fail is mis-estimation of per-session KV demand or pool capacity, and under genuine overload the system still refuses work—without the budgeter, a brief arrival burst can tip the server into a persistent degraded regime with roughly halved throughput. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines
item.description: SlackTier replaces host DRAM-resident Engram n-gram tables with a tiered storage solution utilizing NVMe or RDMA, integrated into the SGLang decode CUDA graph. The approach necessitates specific infrastructure, including NVMe arrays or RDMA-capable networking, and requires implementation within the serving framework to manage prefetch deadlines and caching. Adoption risks include unpredictable latency if input patterns change or if session reuse differs significantly from the evaluated agent and chat traffic. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
item.description: HMRU replaces naive or single-strategy agentic memory retrieval with a training-free hybrid pipeline that jointly improves evidence accessibility and task-aware utilization of retrieved content. It costs additional retrieval and prompt-construction complexity and modest inference overhead, but requires no model training, no fine-tuning infrastructure, and works with third-party APIs. It can fail when the underlying memory store contains stale or low-fidelity biomedical facts, when retrieval surfaces plausible but incorrect evidence that the LLM then trusts, or when conversational histories grow long enough that hybrid scoring still misses relevant turns. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
item.description: Replaces manual expert-driven cycles of model selection, hyperparameter tuning, data curation, and per-device quantization testing with an orchestrator-LLM-driven search that uses real on-device measurements and rule-based rollback. Costs include orchestrator LLM API calls, GPU time for fine-tuning candidates, phone-specific measurement infrastructure across inference engines, and integration complexity of the agentic pipeline. The method can fail on tasks outside the ten evaluated, the adaptive accuracy goal may settle below achievable quality, and results depend on access to target phones, so conclusions may not transfer to devices or engines not measured. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
item.description: Replaces sequential evaluation of nonlinear state space models (and exact parallel Newton with dense Jacobian multiplies) with a parallel Broyden quasi-Newton method using diagonal-plus-low-rank Jacobian approximations built from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation. Costs include maintaining and compressing low-rank updates compatible with parallel scan, plus implementation complexity in reformulating evaluation as root-finding; no foundation-model scale or cluster is required. Convergence degrades when the true Jacobian coupling is not approximately low-rank, when compression error grows, or when block approximation error along the trajectory is large, in which case diagonal quasi-Newton or sequential evaluation may be preferable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Closing the BF16-FP16 Convergence Speed Gap in RL Post-Training with Stochastic Rounding
item.description: Replaces round-to-nearest quantization of FP32 shadow weights to BF16 with stochastic rounding during RL post-training. Costs are limited to a modified quantization step and added implementation complexity, with no stated memory or latency overhead. It can fail if the implementation does not reproduce the claimed convergence or KL benefits on the reader's specific model, dataset, and training stack. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
item.description: The method replaces training a sparse autoencoder on raw model activations with training on activations whose first principal component (massive-activation direction) has been removed, then adding PC1 back to the reconstruction. The cost is a PCA computation over collected activations, a modified training pipeline, and separate handling of the PC1 component, with negligible inference-time impact since SAEs are analysis artifacts. It can fail on models without dominant massive activations (where PC1 removal is unnecessary), if the PCA basis is computed on an unrepresentative activation sample, or if downstream interpretation requires features that partially load on PC1. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Tri-Stack-PIM: A Heterogeneous Multi-Die 3D-Integrated Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Efficient LLM Inference
item.description: The method replaces off-chip DRAM access and host-offloaded nonlinear operations in GPU-based decoding with a three-die stack separating DRAM storage, mature-node PHY/DMA/near-memory logic, and an advanced-node SIMD MAC die, coordinated by a hardware out-of-order scheduler. It costs custom 3D-integrated silicon with hybrid bonding, a dedicated micro-operation scheduler, and architecture-dataflow co-design effort, none of which is purchasable or deployable on existing hardware. It can fail commercially because the results are architectural evaluations rather than measurements of a manufactured part, so yield, thermal, and cost feasibility at production scale remain unvalidated. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
item.description: The method replaces floating-point runtime kernels with an end-to-end exact integer arithmetic path (floating point confined to offline quantization), yielding bit-identical outputs across hardware, instruction sets, and distributed machines, verified via SHA-256 of outputs. It costs substantial storage (e.g., 427 GB of integer codes for a 106B MoE), offers no per-device speed-up (explicitly disclaimed), and confines fidelity to matching the float reference's decisions rather than bit-equal floating intermediates. Adoption risks include decision mismatches versus the float reference on untested inputs (numeric exceptions were measured, not eliminated), storage and memory footprints exceeding single-host RAM, and no guarantee against a dishonest server, which the authors defer to future work. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multi-Objective Scheduling of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows in Cloud Computing
item.description: This technique replaces ad-hoc or single-objective execution strategies for deploying LLM-based multi-agent workflows onto heterogeneous cloud resources. It requires formulating workload scheduling as a multi-objective optimization problem and selecting among genetic or heuristic solvers, which introduces algorithmic complexity and a dependency on accurate latency and cost models of the underlying infrastructure. The approach can fail if the workload characteristics deviate from the modeled assumptions or if the chosen Pareto-optimal solution does not align with actual production priorities for latency, cost, or utilization. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Alania-2: Turkish text-to-speech with instant and fine-tuned voice cloning
item.description: This approach replaces reliance on massive real-world audio corpora and foundation-scale models by training a compact 488M-parameter system on 18,195 hours of teacher-generated synthetic speech (90% of data) combined with deterministic text normalization rules. The costs involve implementing normalization logic, curating the teacher model, and engineering diffusion inference to achieve 32ms first-audio latency. Failures include inability to synthesize alphanumeric strings or loanwords without the normalizer, and instant voice cloning exhibiting 21.9% word omission unless conditioned to continue the reference audio rather than clone from it. 2 independent implementations, 675 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
item.description: The technique replaces recomputing KV caches for shared long prefixes after a model weight update by directly reusing the previous version's cache. It costs nothing in new computation at reuse time, but introduces divergence between reused-cache and native inference behavior, which grows with prefix length in single-token retrieval tasks. It can fail through large retrieval-accuracy losses on some updates and through disagreement in answer content or stopping behavior even when the first generated token matches. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Generalizing Causal Decision-Making: Markov Equivalence, Transportability and Counterfactuals
item.description: The method replaces standard exploration over the full action space in bandit problems with causally pruned action sets derived from graphical criteria, partial transportability bounds, and counterfactual action characterizations. Its cost is the requirement for a partially specified causal model (partial ancestral graphs, source-environment distributions, and prior bounds), plus the implementation of graph-search and dominance-pruning algorithms rather than a drop-in library. It fails when the assumed causal structure or transferred source distributions are misspecified, in which case valid prior bounds and the associated regret guarantee no longer hold and optimal actions may be pruned. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
item.description: Sable replaces trusted, unverifiable inference with a cryptographic argument that a committed integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence bit for bit, using a 31-bit prime constraint system, Reed-Solomon/BLAKE3/BaseFold commitments, and a single-GPU streaming prover. It costs 41-50x serving latency per proved request, requires redefining the model as a deterministic integer function F_O whose greedy output matches BF16 only 86.3% of positions (within 1.6-1.7 points on MMLU/GSM8K), and the proof is not zero-knowledge, so it applies only to open-weight models. It can fail operationally when bit-exact equivalence to the deployed floating-point model is required, since F_O diverges from BF16 outputs at a nontrivial rate and verified results certify the quantized surrogate rather than the original model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
item.description: SinkState replaces dense storage and full per-step rewriting of linear-attention recurrent states with an adaptive low-rank representation using buffered updates, top-subspace local SVD, and asynchronous CPU consolidation. It adds implementation complexity in the inference path: custom state management, rank adaptation logic, and CPU-offload synchronization beyond standard Mamba-SSM or FLA kernels. It can fail if a deployment's layers do not exhibit the assumed low-rank query/key/value concentration, if per-state rank variation makes the adaptive scheme unstable, or if CPU consolidation bandwidth becomes a bottleneck at high batch sizes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
item.description: MaLoRA replaces heuristic adapter-merging coefficients (e.g., uniform averaging, task-arithmetic weights) with a training-free, margin-derived mixing rule for combining independently trained LoRA adapters. It costs only a closed-form coefficient computation per merge, adding no inference memory or latency beyond standard merged-adapter serving, though it presumes access to per-task adapters and margin estimates. It can fail when tasks are not near-orthogonal (the theory's core assumption), when adapters were trained without the relevant regularization regime, or on non-classification tasks such as open-ended generation where margins are undefined. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
item.description: It replaces surrogate drafter training objectives (cross-entropy, KL, total variation, and block-level approximations such as WTV, VSD, DBLast) with an unbiased estimate of expected acceptance length using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization, requiring only a change to the training loss and no change to drafter architecture or inference. The cost is retraining the drafter with a more complex loss, plus the implementation and validation effort of integrating the reference code; inference-time memory and latency are unchanged. It can fail if acceptance-length gains measured under probabilistic serving do not transfer to the reader's target model, drafter, sampling settings, or task mix, and unbiasedness does not guarantee superiority over tuned baselines in every workload. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
item.description: The method replaces fp16 weight storage and single-order multiple-choice evaluation with 6-bit round-to-nearest quantized weights plus averaging over up to four cyclic permutations of answer options. The cost is a multiplicative inference pass increase (up to 4x forward passes) traded against roughly 2.7x memory reduction from 6-bit weights, priced jointly as weight-bytes-read times passes. What can fail: the findings rest on two small models, a simulated quantizer, 300 items per benchmark, and an inconclusive noise control on slot skew, so the +1.8-point anomaly at 6 bits and the cost-matched decision table may not transfer to other models, real quantization kernels, or larger evaluation sets. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SkipLane: Write-Once, Conflict-Free Accumulation for Zero-Skipping CNN Engines on FPGAs
item.description: SkipLane replaces read-modify-write row-buffer accumulation in zero-skipping CNN engines with write-once per-kernel-row lanes that retire finished columns into conflict-free memory banks, summing lanes only at readout. It costs additional FPGA logic (three registers per lane, multiple banks, 21.1k LUTs for six engines) and requires a custom RTL accelerator design rather than commodity hardware. It can fail on layers with short output rows: conv2 reaches only 0.87x dense speed, and all results are RTL/board results on LeNet-5, so gains may not generalize to larger networks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
item.description: Bonbon replaces structure-dependent molecular interaction pipelines (co-folding, docking-based binding-site and affinity prediction, and task-specific supervised models) with zero-shot inference from a frozen protein-ligand sequence foundation model. The cost is dependence on a 1.6B-parameter pretrained model the reader cannot train themselves, plus validation overhead to confirm emergent capabilities transfer to their specific targets; inference itself is lightweight and API-compatible. It can fail on molecular series far from the training distribution, emergent capabilities may not transfer to novel protein families, and the model offers no structural coordinates when atom-level pose information is required. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts Models: Expert Bytes, Kernel Bandwidth and the Best Draft Length
item.description: The method modifies the inference engine's speculative verification pass so that each MoE expert selected by multiple drafted tokens is read from memory once instead of once per token, replacing the standard per-slot expert read in engines such as llama.cpp and MLX-LM. It costs engine-level modifications (the authors patched llama.cpp CUDA and Metal and MLX-LM themselves), a per-model bandwidth calibration of under an hour on one expert operation, and added scheduling complexity in the decoding pass. It can fail because the per-slot kernel often has higher effective bandwidth (r = 0.32 to 0.75), making deduplication slower except in a narrow 5-8 token window or never, and the model's own error bounds were violated at 12 of 48 measured points on Metal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agent Benchmarks Stop Ranking Before They Run Out of Tasks
item.description: Replaces binary pass/fail benchmark aggregation with a clipped log-ratio score against dated human or reference anchors, treating cost as a separate reporting axis. Cost is negligible: it is a re-scoring of existing run artifacts plus anchor selection, requiring no model changes or extra GPU work. It can fail if anchors become stale, if the clipped log-ratio metric is gamed on saturated tasks, or if graded credit masks regressions that pass/fail would surface. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Megrez: A Knowledge-Guided Agent for Formal Mathematics over MK Set Theory
item.description: Megrez replaces manual, ad-hoc formal proof development and retrieval with a knowledge-graph-guided coding agent that uses a feedback-driven tactic loop and a three-check acceptance pipeline. The system requires building and maintaining a source-rebuildable knowledge graph, managing a multi-corpus provider stack, and running continuous compiler checks, which introduces significant infrastructure and operational complexity. Adoption can fail if the curated metadata becomes stale, the proof dependencies are incorrectly mapped, or the acceptance pipeline rejects valid proofs due to statement fidelity or axiom auditing issues. 2 independent implementations, 139 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
item.description: DrugCoding replaces manually orchestrated drug discovery workflows with an LLM agent that plans tasks, routes to specialized scientific models, generates and executes code, and coordinates multi-agent validation. It costs the overhead of maintaining tool interfaces, model routing infrastructure, and multi-agent execution on top of API or local model usage, plus benchmark-specific adaptation. It can fail when scientific tools are misinvoked, when generated code executes incorrectly despite validation, or when the underlying LLM's planning or routing degrades on workflows outside the benchmark distribution. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Do They Do as They Are Told? Investigating Coding Agents' Adherence to Explicit Instructions in Context Files
item.description: The technique replaces the untested assumption that instructions in agent context files (e.g., AGENTS.md) are followed, by operationalizing explicit instructions into executable measurement scripts and auditing agent commits for instruction-level compliance. It costs engineering effort to write and maintain per-instruction checkers, adds a CI or evaluation step, and covers only instructions that are mechanically observable. It can fail through incomplete operationalization, false positives from weakly specified scripts, and polarized adherence where some instruction categories are never respected by specific agents. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
item.description: Replaces manual authoring of OWL ontologies that ground robot kinematics by automating URDF parsing with an LLM plus graph-purging and dual-track tree/chain extraction. Costs are LLM API calls per robot model and integration effort for a robotics ontology pipeline, with no published latency or memory profile relevant to a 24 GB deployment. Failure modes include LLM semantic misclassification of joints and links, taxonomy misalignment on arbitrary user schemas, and graph-purging errors on complex or atypical kinematic structures, all requiring expert validation before use in task allocation. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
item.description: ActiveSecHarness replaces LLM-as-a-judge guardrails and static regex blacklists for tool-using coding agents with deterministic OS/tool guards, HMAC capability tokens, and a 2D taint lattice tracking trust and sensitivity with workspace provenance. The cost is engineering complexity: implementing ring-based permissions, capability tokens, and a provenance ledger is a substantial architectural change to an existing agent harness, not a drop-in filter. It can fail where deterministic policies are incomplete or misconfigured, the N=252 fixture evaluation may not cover novel attack structures, and its perfect ABR/FPR figures are self-reported on a single benchmark without independent replication. 2 independent implementations, 2130 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
item.description: TIGA replaces iterative free-form LLM prompting for taxonomy construction with an explicit-state, tool-grounded decision process using executable editing tools, interaction memory, and a runtime-adaptive policy. It costs substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time relative to prompting baselines. It can fail to dominate on precision measures, and the benefit of the global reviewer component is dataset- and budget-dependent. 2 independent implementations, 41 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
item.description: The method replaces unstructured expert-level pruning or full-model retention in Mixture-of-Experts models by identifying and retaining domain-specialized neurons across expert boundaries using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling. It requires mixed-domain calibration data and preprocessing to compute neuron importance scores, adding implementation complexity compared to magnitude-based pruning. Performance may degrade significantly on out-of-distribution tasks if calibration data does not match production traffic, as neuron specialization was validated on specific academic benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
item.description: It replaces ad hoc prompting of external memory tools and compaction protocols with a single policy post-trained via asynchronous on-policy distillation to use Bash and a persistent workspace as file-based memory across context replacements. The cost is a full post-training pipeline: RL-style long-horizon environments, a frozen teacher with file-operation priors, asynchronous rollout infrastructure, and joint training across five environments, none of which fits a 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. Failure modes include poor transfer when deployment environments lack persistent filesystem access, memory actions that do not generalize beyond the training distribution, and dependence on a teacher whose own file-operation competence bounds what the student can learn. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
item.description: The method replaces purely natural-language skill documents by separating reusable procedural logic into executable, editable programs. It introduces additional complexity through program-aided skill evolution and iterative refinement based on execution feedback. Failures can arise from program bugs, unstable skill updates, or poor generalisation when learned procedures do not transfer across tasks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
item.description: ProofCoder replaces the rigid tactic-generation loop of prior LLM proof systems, where an external controller manages retrieval, proof state, and backtracking, with a coding-agent style loop in which the model reasons continuously and decides when to inspect states, revise fragments, or backtrack. It costs API-level LLM inference plus a Rocq proof-assistant environment; the paper reports roughly half the cost of the baseline, though actual spend depends on model choice and task difficulty. It can fail where formal verification is not part of the workflow, since the method only applies to Rocq/Coq proof construction, and success rates around 60% mean many lemmas still require human proof engineering. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.
