item.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
item.description: The method replaces trusted DiffServ marking and per-flow fair queuing (fq_codel) with a reserved DSCP value for agent traffic plus a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting their declared class, backed by a rate-limited priority queue. The cost is router configuration and classifier deployment on network equipment, plus up to a 12% increase in human-traffic delay and the risk of demoting legitimate flows when the classifier errs. It can fail in practice because most gains came from the separate class rather than verification, a four-feature live classifier missed six spoofers that copied the agent pattern, and the timing feature stopped separating agent from human flows under emulated network delay; all evaluation was synthetic or sandbox-scale. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PARLEY: Evaluating LLM Collaboration Through Cooperative Asymmetric Puzzles
item.description: PARLEY replaces ad hoc, single-metric evaluation of LLM agent pairs with a structured benchmark of asymmetric cooperative puzzles plus the PAC failure taxonomy (Perception, Adaptation, Coordination) for diagnosing collaboration breakdowns. It costs an evaluation harness and API inference spend for conversation rollouts, and the intervention adds taxonomy-derived guidance to agent prompts rather than model changes. Findings may not transfer: results come from GPT-4o pairs on four puzzle tasks, so failure categories and the 10-point gain may shift with different models, domains, or real production tasks. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces flat, lesson-only agent memory (insights distilled from trajectories and later injected without provenance) with lessons linked to per-trajectory success/failure summaries and raw trajectories, letting the agent verify or correct a lesson before acting. Costs include storing trajectories alongside insights, extra retrieval and terminal-tool calls to descend through links when lessons conflict, lack detail, or originate from failed tasks, which adds latency, token spend, and pipeline complexity. Failure modes include corrupted or missing raw trajectories, high retrieval overhead on large memory stores, and residual degradation when summaries omit the evidence needed to catch a wrong lesson. 3 independent implementations, 2261 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces direct writing of episode-derived lessons into persistent agent memory by treating each candidate lesson as a structured hypothesis that is applied only temporarily and tested before commitment. It costs extra inference calls and engineering complexity to construct hypotheses, run target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and maintain a gated memory lifecycle. It can fail if probes are weak or unrepresentative, if verifier feedback is noisy or misaligned, or if the added gating rejects useful updates or still admits harmful ones under distribution shift. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
item.description: EngineAgent replaces manual cross-layer porting of new LLMs into on-device inference engines (conversion, graph construction, operators, hardware backends) with a builder-auditor agent pair guided by a pre-built hierarchy-aware engine index. The cost is an upfront phase of indexing engine abstractions and pre-validating backend build and debugging workflows, plus continued LLM API spending, though reported lower than baseline agents. It can fail on the 25% of tasks not solved end-to-end, when engine dependencies are not captured in the index, or when device-side validation diverges from host expectations. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
item.description: ARE-bench replaces standalone, clean-workspace agent benchmarks with 75 tasks replayed from real researcher sessions and in-progress workspaces, scored by 1,173 binary checklist items covering delivery contracts, general norms, and historical/workspace requirements. The cost is that this is an evaluation artifact rather than a deployable method: using it requires frontier-model API access, reproducing replayed workspaces, and accepting that checklist compilation still involves rubric construction effort. Its own finding indicates what can fail in practice: agents passing roughly 69% of tasks on delivery alone drop to 28.4%–40.0% once historical and workspace constraints are checked, so relying on context-free evaluation will overestimate any agent the reader ships. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
item.description: The method replaces per-task policies and short training runs with one vision-language-action checkpoint trained for 200k steps over 211M demonstration frames, using variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching and stage/task embeddings warm-started across tasks, plus optional routing of hard tasks to a proprietary LLM agent with motion tools. It costs a 200k-step training run on a 100-task demonstration dataset, a custom six-simulator-per-GPU evaluation infrastructure with provenance tracking, and dependence on a closed third-party model (GPT-6 Astra) for a third of the reported gains. It can fail because the learned policy alone succeeds on only a fraction of tasks (0.108 Q on the agent-routed subset), results depend on challenge-specific teleoperation data and simulator tuning that do not transfer to other domains, and the agent-routed component is not reproducible without comparable proprietary model access. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
item.description: Replaces per-step LLM planning in repetitive SOP execution with a code-based workflow whose routing conditions are distilled from logged agent reasoning, so the LLM is no longer called to select each step. Costs a modest drop in completion (93.8% vs 96.8% in production, 75.8% vs 80.6% on tau2-Bench) plus a one-time pipeline of log collection, rule extraction, workflow compilation, and repair rounds on labeled failures. Can fail on out-of-distribution inputs not covered by logged runs, on SOPs that change and invalidate the extracted rules, and when the available training runs are too few or unrepresentative for the repair loop to close the accuracy gap. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.
